project.name: Site Delivery Check
project.problem: Freelance web developers manually compare a finished page with a client brief and lack a compact record of exactly what was checked.
project.user: An independent web developer preparing a small business landing page for client delivery from their own local build.
project.outcome: A reviewed checklist tied to brief quotes and actual browser measurements; reduced preparation effort is a hypothesis to measure.
project.overlayDecision: Briefs and exported evidence may contain client text, so privacy applies. UI and English/Roman Urdu input trigger interface/i18n. Draft latency and browser resource bounds trigger performance. npm, model and runtime trigger dependencies/licensing/distribution. Browser and model jobs trigger concurrency and local operation. Public developer-facing source/demo triggers release review. No billing, auth, financial execution, model training, hosted service, behavioral telemetry, regulated-sector claim, migration or continuity promise is planned.
project.initialUserCountry: Pakistan for any voluntarily recruited tester; broader distribution unknown.
project.dataPolicy: No application history/telemetry; local inference and explicit exports. Scripts intentionally save synthetic evidence. UI reset is not secure erasure of runtime context or downloads.
project.commercialHypothesis: Freelancers might pay for local setup/support or the time saved before delivery. No price, revenue or willingness-to-pay claim is verified.

model.integrity: SHA-256 verified; real V1/V2 inference completed. Runtime reports Q4_K_M and parameter_size2.0B for tag qwen3:1.7b.

repositorySearch.capability: Local brief-to-reviewable check mapping, bounded page inspection, and evidence reports without generated-code execution.
repositorySearch.summary: Adopt the official browser and already downloaded runtime; inspect one exact test-generation comparator. No application repository removes the need for our small review/report workflow. Search results do not establish novelty.
